formulations.label: Granules (tin/sachet)
formulations.strengths: Per 5 g: ispaghula seed 2.6 g, ispaghula husk 0.11 g, senna fruit equivalent to 15 mg hydroxyanthracene glycosides (as sennoside B)
formulations.note: The clinic product (ispaghula with senna granules) is not listed in UK product databases. This UK granule product contains ispaghula seed and ispaghula husk with senna fruit; the clinic record names only ispaghula husk and senna, so check the clinic product's composition and strengths against it before relying on the doses. Contains sucrose (1.04 g per 5 g dose).

src.q: 2.6 g Ispaghula seed ( Plantago ovata Forssk.); 0.11g Ispaghula husk ( Plantago ovata Forssk); 0.34 - 0.66g Tinnevelly Senna fruit ( Cassia angustifolia Vahl), corresponding to 15 mg hydroxyanthracene glycosides calculated as sennoside B.
Each 5g dose contains 1.04g of sucrose

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Short-term use: occasional constipation; bowel regulation in bed-ridden patients; pain-free evacuation with haemorrhoids.

src.q: For short-term use a) in cases of occasional constipation, b) to achieve bowel regulation in bed-ridden patients, c) in cases of haemorrhoids to achieve pain free evacuation.

items.t: Use only if diet change or pure bulk-forming agents fail. Debilitated and/or elderly patients need medical supervision.

src.q: Manevac should only be used if a therapeutic effect cannot be achieved by a change of diet or the administration of pure bulk forming agents.
The treatment of debilitated patients and / or elderly patients requires medical supervision.

items.t: MHRA (stimulant laxatives, including senna): use only if bulk-forming and osmotic laxatives are ineffective.

src.q: stimulant laxatives should only be used if other laxatives (bulk-forming and osmotic) are ineffective

items.t: Adults, elderly and children over 12: 5-10 g (1-2 level spoonfuls or sachets) once daily at night (not immediately before bed-time). Maximum 30 mg hydroxyanthracene glycosides (10 g granules) a day. Use the smallest dose that gives a soft-formed motion.

src.q: One (5g) or two (10g) level measuring spoons to be taken once daily at night.
The maximum daily dose of hydroxyanthracene glycosides is 30 mg.
This product should not be taken immediately prior to bed-time.

items.t: Not for more than 1 week; 2-3 doses in that week are usually enough.

src.q: Not to be used for more than 1 week (see section 4.4). Usually it is sufficient to take this medicinal product up to two to three times during that week.

items.t: Contraindicated under 12 years.

src.q: Use in children below the age of 12 years is contraindicated (see section 4.3)

items.t: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or excipients; children under 12; pregnancy and lactation.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1. Children under 12 years of age. Pregnancy and lactation

items.t: Sudden change in bowel habit persisting over 2 weeks; undiagnosed rectal bleeding; failure to defecate after a laxative.

src.q: Patients with a sudden change in bowel habit that persists for more than 2 weeks Undiagnosed rectal bleeding and failure to defecate following the use of a laxative.

items.t: Possible or existing ileus, intestinal atony, GI stenosis, oesophageal/cardia disease, paralysis of the intestine or megacolon.

src.q: possible or existing bowel obstruction (ileus) intestinal atony abnormal narrowing (stenosis) of the gastrointestinal tract diseases of the oesophagus and cardia paralysis of the intestine or megacolon

items.t: Acute inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, appendicitis), severe dehydration, abdominal pain of unknown origin, dysphagia.

src.q: acute inflammatory bowel disease (e.g. Crohn's disease, ulcerative colitis, appendicitis) severe dehydration (with loss of fluid and electrolytes) abdominal pain of unknown origin dysphagia

items.t: Always take with enough liquid: with too little fluid, bulk-forming agents can cause throat/oesophageal obstruction with choking, and intestinal obstruction.

src.q: When taken with inadequate fluid amounts, bulk forming agents can cause obstruction of the throat and oesophagus with choking and intestinal obstruction.

items.t: With medicines that inhibit peristalsis (e.g. opioids): use only under medical supervision (risk of ileus).

src.q: In order to decrease the risk of gastrointestinal obstruction (ileus) Manevac should be used together with medicinal products known to inhibit peristaltic movement (e.g. opioids,) only under medical supervision.

items.t: Patients on cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmics, QT-prolonging medicines, diuretics, corticosteroids or liquorice root must consult a doctor first.

src.q: Patients taking cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmic medicinal products, medicinal products inducing QT-prolongation, diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids or liquorice root, have to consult a doctor before taking Manevac concomitantly.

items.t: Avoid long-term use (over 1 week): laxative dependence, atonic colon, fluid/electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia. Stop and seek advice if no effect within 3 days or abdominal pain.

src.q: Long-term use of laxatives (more than 1 week) should be avoided.
Prolonged and excessive use may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalance and hypokalaemia.
If the constipation does not resolve within 3 days or if abdominal pain occurs or in cases of any irregularity of faeces, the use of Manevac should be discontinued and medical advice must be sought.

items.t: Contains potent allergens: hypersensitivity can follow oral use or skin contact.

src.q: Manevac contains potent allergens. As a consequence after oral administration or contact with the skin, Manevac may cause hypersensitivity reactions

items.t: Sucrose: fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take.

src.q: Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase-isomaltase insufficiency should not take this medicine.

items.t: May delay absorption of minerals, vitamin B12, cardiac glycosides, coumarins, carbamazepine and lithium: separate from other medicines by ½ to 1 hour.

src.q: Enteral absorption of concomitantly administered medicines such as minerals, vitamins (B12), cardiac glycosides, coumarin derivatives, carbamazepine and lithium may be delayed.
For this reason Manevac should not be taken ½ to 1 hour before or after intake of other medicinal products.

items.t: Antidiabetic therapy may need adjustment (medical supervision); insulin dose may need reducing if taken with meals.

src.q: Diabetic patients should take Manevac only under medical supervision because adjustment of anti-diabetic therapy may be necessary.
If Manevac is taken together with meals by insulin dependent diabetic patients it may be necessary to reduce the insulin dose.

items.t: Thyroid hormones: medical supervision; dose may need adjusting.

src.q: Use of Manevac concomitantly with thyroid hormones requires medical supervision because the dose of the thyroid hormones may have to be adjusted.

items.t: Laxative-induced hypokalaemia: interacts with cardiac glycosides, antiarrhythmics and QT-prolonging medicines; diuretics and corticosteroids may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

src.q: Hypokalaemia (resulting from long-term laxative abuse) potentiates the action of cardiac glycosides and interacts with antiarrhythmic medicinal products
Concomitant use with other medicinal products inducing hypokalaemia (e.g. diuretics, adrenocorticosteroids and liquorice root) may enhance electrolyte imbalance.

items.t: Kidney disorders: possible electrolyte imbalance. With fluid loss where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency), stop and restart only under medical supervision.

src.q: Patients with kidney disorders should be aware of possible electrolyte imbalance.

In patients suffering from fluid loss where dehydration may be harmful (e.g. renal insufficiency, elderly patients) use of the product should be discontinued and only be restarted under medical supervision.

items.t: No hepatic dosing advice. Chronic overdose of anthranoid-containing medicines may cause toxic hepatitis.

src.q: Chronic ingested overdoses of anthranoid containing medicinal products may lead to toxic hepatitis.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated in pregnancy (genotoxicity data for some senna anthranoids).

src.q: The use during pregnancy is contraindicated because of experimental data concerning a genotoxic risk of several anthranoids in Senna

items.t: BUMPS (differs from the SmPC): bulk-forming laxatives such as ispaghula are often tried first and are safe in pregnancy; stimulant laxatives such as senna are tried only when others have not helped.

src.q: are often tried first and are safe in pregnancy.
Stimulant laxatives only tend to be tried when those above have not helped.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated during lactation (rhein passes into milk in small amounts).

src.q: The use during lactation is contraindicated because after administration of anthranoids, active metabolites, such as rhein, were excreted in breast milk in small amounts.

items.t: SPS (differs from the SmPC): ispaghula husk and standardised senna can each be used during breastfeeding.

src.q: Ispaghula husk can be used during breastfeeding.
Standardised senna preparations can be used during breastfeeding.

reproductive.note: UK SmPC: fertility studies not performed.

items.t: Flatulence (usually settles); abdominal pain, spasm and liquid stools (especially irritable colon; reduce dose); harmless yellow or red-brown urine. Frequencies not known.

src.q: Flatulence may occur with the use of Manevac, this generally disappears in the course of the treatment.
Yellow or red-brown (pH dependent) discolouration of urine by metabolites, which is not clinically significant, may occur during the treatment.

items.t: Oesophageal or intestinal obstruction and faecal impaction, especially if swallowed with too little fluid.

src.q: Abdominal distension and risk of intestinal or oesophageal obstruction (e.g. dysphagia) and faecal impaction may occur, particularly if swallowed with insufficient fluid.

items.t: Hypersensitivity: rhinitis, conjunctivitis, bronchospasm and sometimes anaphylaxis.

src.q: hypersensitivity reactions such as rhinitis, conjunctivitis, bronchospasm and in some cases anaphylaxis

items.t: No result within 3 days, abdominal pain or irregular stools: stop and seek medical advice.

src.q: If the constipation does not resolve within 3 days or if abdominal pain occurs or in cases of any irregularity of faeces, the use of Manevac should be discontinued and medical advice must be sought.

items.t: Sit upright. Place the granules dry on the tongue and swallow without chewing with a glass of water or other liquid; keep up fluid intake.

src.q: The patient should be sitting in an upright position prior to administration of the granules.
should be placed dry on the tongue and, without chewing or crushing, swallowed with a glass of water

items.t: Keep ½ to 1 hour between this and other medicines.

src.q: An interval of half an hour to one hour should be kept after taking another medicinal product.

items.t: Always take with plenty of liquid; stop and seek help if chest pain, vomiting, or difficulty swallowing or breathing.

src.q: Symptoms can be chest pain, vomiting, or difficulty in swallowing or breathing.

items.t: Do not take immediately before going to bed.

src.q: This product should not be taken immediately prior to bed-time.
